baseline.note: remaining_failures are migrations SQLite cannot apply (mostly PostgreSQL-only DDL). Objects they would create are absent from this baseline, so a gap verdict resting on such an object is weak.

oracles: 1. SQLite replay — every migration the runner actually applies, then the shadowed entry against a throwaway copy, diffing normalised sqlite_master DDL.
2. Live PostgreSQL — information_schema.tables/columns + pg_indexes on the local icdev database (read-only).

3. tools/db/schema/pg_consolidated.sql — what bootstrap_pg.py loads on a FRESH PostgreSQL database. This, not the chain, is how a new PG deployment gets its schema, so it is the oracle that decides whether a chain gap is deployable harm.
4. Declaring-source scan — grep for CREATE TABLE/INDEX over tools/ outside tools/db/migrations, to find canvases and reflexes that create tables at app startup and so cover a chain gap on SQLite too.

tool_defect_found_and_fixed.what: build_baseline() did not pin ICDEV_DB_PATH while the migration chain ran.
tool_defect_found_and_fixed.why_it_matters: A migration whose up() does `conn = get_connection()` discards the connection MigrationRunner hands it and resolves the environment instead. 61 tables — sg_conflict_events among them — were written to the repo's data/icdev.db instead of the baseline, so the baseline was short of schema the chain really does create and a shadowed entry declaring the same table scored a gap it is not. _apply_py already guarded the replay half; the baseline half was unguarded, and the baseline is the oracle every verdict is measured against.
tool_defect_found_and_fixed.effect_on_this_audit: baseline 2371 -> 2539 objects, applied 254 -> 256. 055_sg_conflict_events_cyber_op dropped from 'new table sg_conflict_events + 5 indexes' to '4 columns + 1 index'. Verdict totals were unchanged at 17/3, but one verdict rested on wrong evidence.
tool_defect_found_and_fixed.fix: tools/db/shadowed_migration_replay.py::build_baseline now runs the chain inside _pinned_db_path(db_path); mirrored to icdev/. Regression test: tests/db/test_shadowed_migration_replay.py::test_baseline_captures_a_migration_that_opens_its_own_connection

limits: remaining_failures=57 — migrations SQLite cannot apply. A gap verdict resting on an object one of those would have created is weak; none of the 20 rests on one (checked: every declared table was traced to its declaring migrations).
Audited tools/db/migrations. icdev/tools/db/migrations is a separate tree with 78 shadowed entries; all 20 audited entries exist in both.

PostgreSQL CHECK-constraint widening is invisible to a SQLite replay (019 skips its PG branch outright). Both widening entries here were checked directly against pg_constraint and the snapshot instead.
